tasks.title: Letters one by one
tasks.statement: Print each letter of the word «привет» on a separate line. Use a for loop over the string.
tasks.hint: for ch in word: print(ch) — on each pass, ch is the next letter.

tasks.title: Countdown
tasks.statement: Print the numbers from 5 down to 1, each on its own line, and at the end the line «Старт!». Use a while loop and do not forget to decrease the counter.
tasks.hint: while n > 0: print n, then n -= 1. «Старт!» comes after the loop, without indentation.

tasks.title: Squares of numbers
tasks.statement: Print the squares of the numbers from 1 to 5, each on its own line. Get the numbers through range.
tasks.hint: range(1, 6) — six is not included. Inside the loop: print(i * i).

tasks.title: Sum from 1 to n
tasks.statement: Write a function sum_to(n) that returns the sum of all integers from 1 to n inclusive. Compute it with a loop and an accumulator, not with a formula. For n = 0 the sum is 0.
tasks.hint: for i in range(1, n + 1): total += i — the right bound of range has to be shifted by one.
tasks.starter:
def sum_to(n):
    total = 0
    # loop with an accumulator
    return total

tasks.title: Odd numbers only
tasks.statement: Print the odd numbers from 1 to 10, each on its own line. Skip the even ones with the continue command.
tasks.hint: if i % 2 == 0: continue — after it, only the odd numbers reach print.

tasks.title: Factorial
tasks.statement: Write a function factorial(n): the product of all integers from 1 to n. For n = 0 the result is 1. The accumulator for a product starts at one, not at zero.
tasks.hint: for i in range(1, n + 1): result *= i. Zero gives an empty loop and the answer 1, just as needed.
tasks.starter:
def factorial(n):
    result = 1
    # loop with an accumulator
    return result

tasks.title: First digit in a string
tasks.statement: Write a function first_digit(s) that returns the first digit character of the string s (as a string too). If there are no digits, return None. Leave the loop as soon as a digit is found. The method ch.isdigit() will help you check a character.
tasks.hint: Inside the loop: if ch.isdigit(): return ch — return also ends the loop at once.

tasks.title: Word backwards
tasks.statement: Write a function reverse_word(s) that returns the string s written backwards: «привет» becomes «тевирп». Build the result with a loop, attaching each next letter to the BEGINNING of the accumulator. You may not use the ready-made slice [::-1].
tasks.hint: result = ch + result — the new letter goes in front of everything accumulated.

tasks.title: How many pairs
tasks.statement: Write a function count_pairs(n): how many pairs of numbers (i, j) exist with 1 <= i < j <= n. Go through the pairs with two nested loops and count them with a counter.
tasks.hint: for i in range(1, n + 1): for j in range(i + 1, n + 1): count += 1 — the inner loop starts at i + 1.
